plain: The contract between a client and an asset manager for a segregated mandate.
technical: Sets the benchmark, investment guidelines, fees, reporting obligations, liability terms and how either side can terminate.
why_it_matters: It defines the floor of what the manager must do; coverage staff need to know what was actually agreed before promising anything.

plain: A long standard set of questions a client or consultant asks a manager about its firm, people, process, risk controls and operations.
technical: Answers are compared across managers and kept on file; inconsistencies between a DDQ and marketing material are a common research finding.
why_it_matters: Juniors often help assemble and check DDQ answers; accuracy and consistency here are trust made visible.

plain: The database where a firm records its clients, contacts, meetings, notes and open actions.
technical: Holds call notes and decision history with access controls so confidential client information reaches only those who need it.
why_it_matters: It is how relationship knowledge becomes organisational knowledge and survives staff changes.

plain: The risk that someone acting on your behalf follows their own interests instead of yours.
technical: Arises wherever a principal cannot fully observe an agent whose incentives differ; in asset management there is a chain from members to trustees to consultants and managers.
why_it_matters: It locates where conflicts of interest can arise for a coverage professional paid by the manager.

plain: One side of a deal knows more than the other.
technical: Investment management resembles a credence good: quality is hard to judge even after purchase because returns mix skill and luck.
why_it_matters: Much of a coverage role is transferring information credibly so the client can rely on it.

plain: What it costs a client to change provider, beyond the price of the new one.
technical: Includes transition trading costs, legal and operational set-up, time out of the market and governance effort. Neutral about quality: they protect good and bad incumbents alike.
why_it_matters: Retention caused by switching costs is not evidence of client satisfaction.

plain: The time and money it takes to find and assess alternatives.
technical: In institutional investing: RFPs, consultant research, presentations, operational and legal review, committee time.
why_it_matters: An existing relationship lowers the cost of the client's next decision, which is legitimate only if the incumbent would survive an open comparison.

plain: A pension scheme pays an insurer a premium and the insurer takes on paying some or all of the pensions.
technical: In a buy-in the policy is an asset of the scheme; in a buyout the insurer issues policies to members and the scheme can wind up. Scheme assets are used to pay the premium.
why_it_matters: It is the commonest case where the best client outcome ends an asset manager's mandate.

plain: The danger that something valuable depends on one individual.
technical: Applies to portfolio managers (the strategy) and to coverage staff or client contacts (the relationship). Consultants often treat a departure as a trigger for review.
why_it_matters: Explains why firms want multiple contacts and written records for every client.

plain: Ask whether the client would choose the manager again in a fresh, fully informed competition.
technical: A reasoning device used in this dossier (not an industry standard term) to separate retention that reflects value from retention that reflects inertia.
why_it_matters: Gives a concrete way to challenge the claim that retention proves a good relationship.
